session_4.result:
I added both commands and committed them as a53ff1b. The full suite passes (17 tests).

- **`dedupe`**: among active tasks with exactly the same title, it keeps the one with the earliest `due_at` and archives the rest. If two have the same `due_at`, it keeps the lower id. It uses soft-delete, so it never hard-deletes, and it prints how many it archived.
- **`copy ID`**: it creates a task titled `<title> (copy)` with the same `due_at` as the original. The title goes through `normalize_title()` in the CLI, so `create_task` is untouched. A missing id prints "no such task".

If the original title is already close to 80 characters, `normalize_title()` truncates the combined title and the "(copy)" suffix can be cut off. I left it that way because the conventions require normalizing every stored title.

The new code is in `tinytasks/api.py` and `tinytasks/cli.py`, and the tests are in `tests/test_api.py`. I didn't touch `delete_task` or the `delete` command. The already-deleted `__pycache__` files in your git status were not part of the commit.
